passage:
Uday had been seeing Rhea for two months, and he wanted her to come to the Pune flat for dinner on Saturday and stay late. He had almost just done it, because Harsha never said anything about anything. But that morning he caught himself: silence wasn't the same as being fine.

Over tea he said, "Rhea's coming Saturday evening. Are you okay with that? And should we agree on a rule for guests, like telling each other a day ahead?"

Harsha lowered the newspaper. "Honestly, I have a design deadline Saturday and I'd like the flat quiet till nine. After that's fine."

"Done. And when your cousins visit, I get the same warning."

They wrote "Guests: message a day before. Quiet hours 10 pm" on the fridge whiteboard. Uday felt lighter, and a bit silly for nearly skipping it.

qa.q: What did Uday and Harsha write on the fridge whiteboard?
qa.a: "Guests: message a day before. Quiet hours 10 pm."

qa.q: Why did Uday decide to ask Harsha instead of just inviting Rhea?
qa.a: He realised that Harsha's silence didn't mean being fine, and felt a bit silly for nearly skipping the conversation.

qa.q: What does the whiteboard rule do for the two flatmates?
qa.a: It makes expectations clear for both, so neither has to assume the other doesn't mind.

qa.q: What did Harsha need that Uday might not have known?
qa.a: A quiet flat until nine on Saturday because of a design deadline.

grounding: Uday wants to bring his partner over and agrees guest and quiet-hour rules with his roommate beforehand instead of assuming.

passage:
"Rehana, got a sec?" Dolma leaned on the door frame of their room. "Tashi's in town this weekend. Would it be okay if he came over on Saturday afternoon?"
Rehana looked up from her notes. "Thanks for asking first. What time?"
"Maybe two to six? We'd just watch something, make momos."
"Saturday afternoon is my study block. I've got a mock on Monday."
"Oh. Right." Dolma paused. "Would the common room work for us instead? Or Sunday?"
"Sunday after lunch is perfect. I'll be at my aunt's."
"Great. And if you're back early, just walk in. It's your room too."
"Can we make it a thing? Guests only with a day's notice, and nobody stays the night."
"Yes. Same for you."
"I don't have a Tashi."
"Yet."
Rehana threw a pen at her. "Bring me two momos."

qa.q: Why did Dolma pause after hearing about the mock?
qa.a: She felt a little disappointed but considerate, realising her plan clashed with Rehana's study time.

qa.q: Which rules did Dolma and Rehana agree on?
qa.a: Guests only with a day's notice and nobody staying the night, for both of them.

qa.q: How does Rehana feel about being asked first?
qa.a: Respected; she thanks Dolma and happily suggests Sunday instead.

grounding: Shows wanting a partner to visit and agreeing with a roommate beforehand on guests and quiet time.

passage:
Last November I made my roommate Tsering sleep in the common room, and at first I didn't even notice.
Vijay had come from Jaipur for two days. I assumed Tsering wouldn't mind; she's easygoing, and she'd said "sure, whatever" once when I mentioned it weeks before. So I didn't ask again. We had the room, the music, the late dinner.
At eleven Tsering came back from her night lab, saw us, and said, "Oh, I'll go." She left with her pillow. In the morning I found her asleep on the common-room sofa, her lab coat for a blanket.
I felt awful. A "sure, whatever" weeks earlier wasn't agreement for that night.
We talked properly that evening. Now there's a paper on the cupboard: guests need two days' notice, nobody stays past ten on weekdays, and the room is for sleeping whenever either of us needs it.
— Mehak

qa.q: Where did Mehak find Tsering asleep in the morning?
qa.a: On the common-room sofa, with her lab coat for a blanket.

qa.q: How did Mehak feel on finding Tsering there?
qa.a: Awful and guilty, realising the old "sure, whatever" wasn't agreement for that night.

qa.q: What rules did Mehak and Tsering agree on?
qa.a: Two days' notice for guests, nobody past ten on weekdays, and the room is for sleeping whenever either needs it.

qa.q: How might Tsering have felt coming back from her night lab?
qa.a: Tired and pushed out of her own room, too polite to object.

grounding: Illustrates assuming a roommate does not mind a guest, the cost of not asking, and agreeing on rules beforehand.
